name: "Change: 40 Years of SOM London,” a special exhibition exploring design as a cultural practice
description: Enjoy one of two exclusive tours of a special exhibition, "Change," celebrating SOM London’s 40th anniversary and SOM’s 90th anniversary worldwide. Discover rare insights into the work of the globally renowned architecture, engineering and urban planning practice, and explore how innovative design, technology, materials and construction are shaping a more resilient and sustainable future.

name: 'Stories of Belonging' Film Screening
description:
Stories of Belonging – It Takes Courage, is a short film by Halyna Skvortsova, which explores how different waves of migration have shaped Lewisham, featuring voices from the Windrush Generation and Vietnamese, African, Eastern European, Afghan, and Ukrainian communities. 

The screening takes place in the new SHAPES Lewisham community space, for creatives to meet, work, learn and collaborate.
address: SHAPES Lewisham, Studio 1 Carriage Way, Octavius Street, SE8 4BY

name: 1-4 Suffolk Street: Uni of Notre Dame & G.K Chesterton
description: Built for the United Universities Club, 1-4 Suffolk Street  is now home to the University of Notre Dame and its G.K Chesterton Collection. Visitors will be able to enjoy both this Edwardian listed building and the unique collection within.

name: 1.20 Oxo Tower Wharf
description: Carreducker bespoke shoemakers and Shoe & Leather School is located at Unit 1.20, one of 25 workshop and retail units in Oxo Tower Wharf. It overlooks the courtyard towards the Bargehouse building from the first floor walkway and is a multi-purpose space used as a workshop, showroom and teaching space.
address: Unit 1.20, The Courtyard, Oxo Tower Wharf, SE1 9PH

name: 15 Edge Hill
description: New build rear extension to Victorian house, entailing extensive remodelling of ground floor to create a large open plan flow-through living, dining and kitchen space. Close integration with the garden is achieved by careful design of levels and paving surfaces.

name: 1930s Bloomsbury walking tour
description: The leafy Georgian streets of Bloomsbury were shaken up in the 1930s by a new wave of development, from great academic institutions to speculative flats for modern urban living, plus probably the most stylish car showroom in London. We'll explore the range of 1930s architectural styles used in some famous and not so famous buildings, and even take a peek inside where we can.
address: Tottenham Court Road, outside the Dominion Theatre, W1T 7AQ

name: 2 Belgrave Road: Victorian house with Luis Barragán inspired interior
description:
A Luis Barragán inspired design for the interior of a typical late Victorian house in East London. 
The use of bold vivid colour banishes the sterility that can accompany modernism without the loss of its hallmark simplicity and elegant line. This approach can be accommodated within houses whose external architecture has a very different heritage. Its achievement does not require a big budget

name: 22 Parkside AKA Roger's House
description: Built as a private house for his parents, the project encapsulates Rogers' vision of a home built using industrially manufactured components. As such it was seen as a prototype for mass affordable housing. Opening for the Festival in association with The Wimbledon Society

name: 3D Printing at Design District
description: Step inside Champion 3D’s working 3D printing studio at Greenwich Peninsula’s Design District. Visitors can see FDM 3D printers in action, handle different printed materials, explore finished models and learn how digital designs become physical objects.
address: 10 Monro Way, Unit 1.1, Building A4, Greenwich, SE10 0EJ

name: 6 Moretown (Gensler London Studio)
description: A contemporary adaptation of a 1980s office building, and home of global design firm Gensler. Each level of the building is connected by a structural timber facade and set of stairs, and the new 5th floor cantilevers from the roof.

name: 72 Kynaston Road
description:
72 Kynaston Road, N16, is a typical Stoke Newington two storey terraced house.
A simple side return extension expands the kitchen/dining area and connects it to the reception rooms.
What stands out in this design are a generous oriel window seat on to the garden, a bespoke kitchen finished in cherry wood, and the clients bold choice of floor tile.
address: 72 Kynaston Road, Stoke Newington, Hackney, N16 0ED

name: A Ruskinian Walk Through Shared Heritage
description: Ruskinian walk from RIBA award-winning Chiswick Business Park, Gunnersbury Triangle Nature Reserve through South Acton Estate, birthplace of artist Patrick Caulfield; Woodlands Park Ice House; to home of William Willett, initiator of Daylight Saving Time.
address: Building 3, Chiswick Business Park, 566 Chiswick High Road, W4 5YA

name: All Saints Carshalton
description: 12C south aisle and former chancel. Blomfield nave, chancel, baptistry. Kempe glass, Bodley reredos and screen, spectacular Comper decorations, monuments and brasses, award-winning lighting scheme, fine modern benches.

name: All Saints Church, Edmonton
description: Listed Grade ll* and celebrating its 890th year, All Saints Church  has aspects of the fabric dating back to at least early C12 with further modification and additions in the 15th, 17th and 19th centuries.  Charles and Mary Lamb lived on Church Street, where the church is situated and are buried in the Garden of Remembrance within the churchyard.
address: All Saints Church, Church Street, N9 9AT

name: All Saints Church, Kenley
description:
All Saints was founded in 1871 and is proud to touch the lives of many people in the community through outreach and mission.
The church building is Grade 2 listed and is both beautiful and traditional in style.

name: All Saints Church, Upper Norwood
description:
Historical connections:
Vice Admiral Fitzroy(grave within Church Grounds),
Charles Darwin,
Crystal Palace Great Exhibition,
Camille Pissarro (Painter exhibits National Gallery),
Charles Dickens,
(Grave within Church grounds),
Isambard Kingdom Brunel,
Felix Mendelssohn, Marie Tussauds to name but a few. 
Famous artist Camille Pissarro painted local scenes.
address: All Saints Church, Church Road, SE19 3EP

name: An ideal city tour with a landscape architect
description: Moving through the King’s Cross area, the tour explores how green spaces shape everyday life. Walk with a landscape architect to see how design intentions are maintained, adapted, or reinterpreted by the people who use them. By speaking with designers, planners and local residents as part of the tour research, the tour captures stories that reveal how public spaces are imagined, experienced and shared.
address: IFO (Bird Cage) art installation, Battle Bridge Place, N1C 4TB

name: Argentine Ambassador's Residence
description: During the Open House Festival people will have the unique opportunity to explore the historic mansion.  Opening its doors on this special occasion, visitors will enjoy unprecedented access to the Argentine Ambassador's Residence in the UK and explore a glimpse of our culture through an art exposition of different Argentine artists.

name: Armourers' Hall
description: Late Georgian Livery Hall rebuilt in 1839. Highlights include the main Hall, featuring a stunning 1870s lantern ceiling, and displays of historic arms and armour throughout the building.

name: Avery Hill Winter Garden
description: The Avery Hill Winter Garden is a remarkable Victorian glasshouse set within the historic Avery Hill estate in southeast London. Built in the late 19th century, it was once home to an extensive collection of exotic plants and remains one of London’s largest surviving Victorian winter gardens.

name: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
description: Europe’s first traditional Hindu temple is a masterpiece of exquisite Indian craftsmanship. Using 5,000 tonnes of Italian and Indian marble and the finest Bulgarian limestone, it was hand-carved in India before being assembled in London.

name: Barnsbury Flat
description: Renovated by Fynn Architects, this early Victorian flat in the Barnsbury Conservation Area has been reconfigured for a young family. The previous layout left the kitchen stranded in a cramped, pokey room at the rear, so the project brings it forward into the front room and reworks the layout around how the family actually lives, adding a new WC and a nursery for the new arrival.

name: Bazalgette Mausoleum
description:
Portland stone mausoleum of Sir Joseph Bazalgette, composed of an obelisk above a square rusticated base, with steps leading down to the arched entrance of the vault.

Originally built for a different man, John Anthony Rucker, Bazalgette updated the mausoleum to its current look in c.1886.
address: St Mary's Church, 30 St Mary's Road, Wimbledon, SW19 7BP

name: Benjamin Franklin House
description:
Just steps from Trafalgar Square is Benjamin Franklin House, the world's only remaining Franklin home.

For nearly sixteen years between 1757 and 1775, Benjamin Franklin – scientist, diplomat, philosopher, inventor, and Founding Father of the United States – lived behind its doors.

Built circa 1730, we are a Grade I listed house, with largely original flooring and wall paneling.

name: Bethlehem Chapel Richmond upon Thames
description: An independent Calvinistic chapel on the east side of Church Terrace in Richmond, London. Built in 1797, the small 1-storey stuccoed building is Grade II* listed. It still has its original galleried interior with pews and pulpit.
address: Bethlehem Chapel, Church Terrace, Richmond upon Thames , TW10 6SE

name: Billingsgate Roman House & Baths
description: Some of London's best Roman remains, comprising late 2C house with a 3C bath house built within its courtyard. First discovered in 1848.

name: Birds Portchmouth Russum Architects  - Open Office
description: The office is an extraordinary gallery of sublime hand drawings and exquisite models of uniquely joyous architectural projects developed over 35 years that have been exhibited regularly at the Royal Academy Summer Show and in exhibitions around the world. Drop in and the founding directors will be on hand to explain and discuss the wonderful exhibits.
address: Unit 11 , Union Wharf., 23 Wenlock Road, N1 7SB

name: Bloomsbury marginalia – working-class lives in Bloomsbury
description: Discover the many ordinary and working class people who lived and worked in Bloomsbury. Join me on a tour of Bloomsbury's mews and back streets to learn about slum quarters and social housing, street traders and factories, listening to marginalised voices from the time along the way.
address: The Bloomsbury Hotel, 16-22 Great Russell Street, WC1B 3NN

name: Boston Manor House
description: Boston Manor House is a Jacobean House built for Lady Mary Reade in 1623 and later owned by the Clitherow family from the 1670s until the 1920s. The House is now open to the public with free entry six days a week. Its beautifully restored historic interiors, including breath-taking ornate plasterwork, are joined by two community exhibition galleries, meeting rooms and an attractive modern café.
address: Boston Manor House, Boston Manor Road, Brentford, TW8 9JX

name: Brandon Centre
description: West Kentish Town Conservation Area. Brandon Cadbury (of the famous philanthropic chocolatiers) was so impressed with our founder and our young people's services that he donated our building. As a thank-you, we named the charity after him in 1984.
address: 26 Prince of Wales Road , Kentish Town, NW5 3LG

name: Brick Sixty Studio
description:
A rare chance to see behind the scenes at the newly located Brick Sixty Studio on Roman Road, London.

This stock brick Victorian shop with accommodation above, was refurbished this year by Architectural Workshop. Now home to Brick Sixty, who design and make products in the form of the much-loved London brick and are looking to support local makers & craft in the UK with the new space.
address: Brick Sixty, 469 Roman Rd, E3 5LX, E3 5LX

name: Bridge House
description: Bridge House is a mixed-use building by Studioshaw with 40 apartments and commercial space. The design is a new vernacular for multi-unit residential development in London. All apartments are dual-aspect and share a rooftop garden, with balconies over the canal and new public square. The facade is made from concrete elements cast only 750m from site. The building's structure is its architecture.

name: Brixton Windmill
description: A wonderful reminder of Brixton's rural past and inner London's last working mill. Built in 1816 by the Ashby family who produced flour until 1934.  Restored to working order 2011. Producing flour today thanks to our volunteer millers.

name: Calamity and civility: contrasts in Clerkenwell
description: Tranquil Clerkenwell, so close to the bustling City, has a distinct character and intriguing history. Once centred around great religious houses, the area has been the scene of fierce rebellion, innovative architecture, and major commerce.

name: Canada House
description: Canada's diplomatic home in the United Kingdom, the revitalised Canada House serves as a showcase for the very best of Canadian art and design in the 21C.

name: Carshalton Water Tower and Historic Gardens
description: Early 18C Grade II listed building incorporating plunge bath with Delft tiles, orangery, saloon and pump chamber with part-restored water wheel. Hermitage and sham bridge in grounds.

name: Charing Cross Library
description: The building has had many incarnations since its construction in the 1890s as a woolen warehouse.   It became a home to the Italian Benevolent Society, then a fascist club, a serviceman's club, and now a library with the largest publicly accessible collection of Chinese language books in the UK.  View the temporary exhibition on the Matteotti Affair.

name: Charlton House & Gardens
description: Charlton House is one of the UK's few remaining Jacobean manor homes and a Grade-I listed building. Find it in Charlton Park, southeast London. Built between 1607-1612 for Sir Adam Newton, tutor to Henry, Prince of Wales, many original features still exist. They include red brick with stone dressings, oak staircases, panelled rooms, strapwork ceilings, and original fireplaces.
address: Charlton House & Gardens, Charlton Road, SE7 8RE

name: Christ Church
description: The church is designed in the Gothic style, with a semicircular barrel-vaulted ceiling, a highly carved chancel screen and magnificent stained glass windows, notably the large West window, depicting Christ the King enthroned in heaven.

name: Church of the Annunciation
description: Fine Victorian church with large mosaic and painted reredos, screen and wall paintings and some unusual glass. Arts and crafts decoration by Nathaniel Westlake and Salviati Bros.

name: City Hall
description: The sustainable headquarters of the Mayor of London and London Assembly located in the Royal Docks, Newham. The docks are re-emerging as a commercial and cultural hub, and an exciting new waterfront.

name: City Information Centre
description: London's main tourist information centre is clad in a specially manufactured system of 220 pre-finished stainless steel panels. The subtly reflective surface provides a striking counterpoint to St Paul's.

name: City of Westminster Archives Centre
description: Modern red brick building purpose-built to house the City of Westminster's historic records. Opportunity to visit the conservation studio and see treasures of the archives.

name: Company Drinks Pavilion and Garden
description:
Company Drinks is a local drinks enterprise and community hub based in Barking Park. Our space includes a beautiful community garden and a former outdoor bowls pavilion that's now home to social areas, a community kitchen, and creative making spaces.
Our Annual Community Open Day on 12th September is a fun, family-friendly free event with workshops, taster sessions and tours of the site.
address: Outdoor Bowls Pavilion, Barking Park, Longbridge Road Barking

name: Corbett Community Library
description: Visit the Grade II listed Corbett Community Library building. This beautifully preserved Edwardian building is rich in architectural character and heritage, featuring , an impressive dome, ornate door handles, some stained glass and a historic brass plaque. Discover the history and craftsmanship of this remarkable community landmark during your visit.
address: Corbett Community Library, 103 Torridon Road, SE6 1RQ

name: Crown Court Church of Scotland
description: A Church of Scotland in London, home to the longest-established Presbyterian congregation in London, worshipping in this location in Covent Garden since 1719. The current building is red brick with Portland stone dressings in a restrained, finely crafted Free Style. Three storeys, recessed slated attic, mullioned and transomed windows. Fine stained glass, most of which is by Farrar Bell.

name: Croydon Curiosity Rover
description: As part of Open House 2026 in Croydon, visit an exhibition of our summer programme with Creative Quests: Curiosity Rover, and try some creative missions of your own! Part art studio, part community hub and part roaming spacecraft, collect quests to explore Croydon through noticing, movement, nature and imagination.

name: Croydon Minster
description: Medieval style church rebuilt by Sir George Gilbert Scott after 1867 fire. Tower & south porch are 15C. Large nave with open timber-work roof leads to chancel dominated by superb stained glass window & rich alabaster reredos.

name: Croydon Urban Room
description:
The Croydon Urban Room is a space to talk about the past, present and future of the Croydon town centre. Through conversa­tions, stories, exhibitions and events, the Urban Room brings together the views of those who live, work and visit the area to create a shared vision of the future and test new uses live in action. 

See our website for further details of specific events.

name: Crystal Palace Subway
description: Come and join us to explore the beautifully restored Subway. The Subway was opened in 1865 to give train passengers more direct (and less hilly!) access to the famous Crystal Palace.  We are delighted to welcome Southwark and District Model Railway Club, who will be bringing their large model of Crystal Palace High Level Station - the first time it's been shown in the Subway!
address: Crystal Palace Parade, Crystal Palace, SE19 2BA

name: Dagenham Parish Church
description: The oldest surviving building in Dagenham, a grade 2 listed church building.  With historical memorials including a Jan van Nost sculpture.
address: Dagenham Parish Church, Church Lane, Dagenham, RM10 9UL

name: De Lane Lea Studios, 75 Dean Street
description: Step inside the legendary De Lane Lea Studios at 75 Dean Street, now home to the Museum of Soho, and discover the stories, sounds and creativity that have shaped this remarkable neighbourhood. As part of Open House, enjoy a programme of talks, screenings and conversations celebrating Soho's unique spirit of innovation, diversity and cultural influence.

name: Dorich House Museum
description: Dorich House is the former studio home of the sculptor Dora Gordine and her husband the Hon. Richard Hare, a scholar of Russian art and literature. Now Grade II listed, the building was completed in 1936, to Gordine’s design, and is an exceptional example of a modern studio house by a woman artist.
address: Dorich House Museum, 67 Kingston Vale, SW15 3RN

name: Dr Johnson's House
description: Fine example of an early 5-floor Queen Anne town house with original panelling, open staircase and unique 'swinging panels' on the open-plan first floor. Johnson compiled his famous 'Dictionary of the English Language' (1755)  here.

name: Ealing Common Walk
description: Saturday 12th September. Meet at the Iron Duke sculpture for a 2.00 p.m. start. Ends at 3.30 p.m. with refreshments at All Saints Church. Walk along the perimeter of  Ealing Common, taking in the range of architectural styles. Highlights: the home of a Wimbledon champion and the death mask of a prime minister.
address: at Hanger Lane end of Inglis Road, behind Iron Duke train sculpture

name: East Croydon History Walk
description: Historic walking tour of East Croydon led by a native. Those who come along are welcome to contribute their memories.  Marvel at one of the oldest electricity sub-stations in Croydon. Tour ends at the iconic One Croydon, the "Thru'penny Bit" office block designed by Seifert in the 1960s.  Join us for a drink afterwards in a Victorian hostelry.
address: The Cricketers, 107 Addiscombe Road, Croydon, CR0 6SG

name: Eco Punk
description: Eco Punk consists of a generous rear extension plus the remodel of an Edwardian house located in a conservation area. The new layout unlocks the spatial potentials. Besides beautifully crafted lounges, dining and utility areas, there is a kitchen that forms the centre piece. The latter is designed for a professional chef. An elegant, natural material palette ties the scheme together.

name: Edmonton – the making of a north London suburb: past, present & future
description: Edmonton has been described as a working class suburb but there are now signs of growing affluence, a result of regeneration and some might say the neighbourhood is ripe for gentrification. The walk will explore a variety of neighbourhoods.
address: Entrance to Silver Street Station (Platform 1, London bound side)

name: Energy and Sustainability through time: King's Cross
description: Join this walking tour to explore London's energy history and its impact on sustainability. Visit the King's Cross canals to see old and new infrastructure. Topics include London's carbon footprint, quantifying health benefits from green infrastructure, and the role of the built environment in meeting the net zero targets. Discover how London’s past has shaped its sustainable future.
address: Outside German Gymnasium Restaurant, 1 King's Blvd, N1C 4BU

name: Estorick Collection of Modern Italian Art
description: The Estorick Collection is housed in a beautiful Georgian building previously known as Northampton Lodge. Today, the museum comprises six galleries over three floors, as well as a library, offices, a café and bookshop.

name: Family Day in the City
description: Once again City of London cultural sites have pulled together to create an Open House offering for families. Join Guildhall Art Gallery, the Insurance Museum, London Mithraeum Bloomberg SPACE, St Paul’s Cathedral and Dr Johnson’s House to celebrate architecture, heritage and placemaking in the City. Pick up a map or join the walking bus to explore it all.
address: Guildhall Art Gallery, Guildhall Yard, EC2V 5AE

name: Florentia Village
description: Ready to see an industrial estate that is anything but grey and boring? Developed by General Projects and designed by Turner Works, Florentia Village combines workshops, studios and light industrial space with shared courtyards and open walkways. Join architectural tours, browse a local makers market, and drop into open studios for creative talks and workshops.
address: 108 Vale Road, Harringay Warehouse Distrcit, N4 1TD

name: Former Edmonton Girls' Charity School
description: The former Charity School was constructed in 1793, by Obadiah Legrew, who also purchased the adjoining no.24 Church Street, part of the surviving earlier 18th century range, to create a small cottage for the School Mistress.
address: Charity School Hall (next door to 24 Church Street), N9 9DU

name: Foster + Partners
description: We're excited to open up our London campus. Foster + Partners is a global studio for sustainable architecture, urbanism, engineering and design, founded by Norman Foster in 1967. Hosted across several buildings, the public can explore the studio, take part in interactive exhibitions and workshops, and gain an insight into the wide range of disciplines and projects across the globe.

name: Founders' Hall
description: Founders’ Hall is the home of the Worshipful Company of Founders (one of the City’s ancient livery companies). Built in the 1980s with a striking and eclectic design, the Hall preserves historic traits whilst embracing modern ideas. Drop in during Open House to explore its treasures, meet members, and enjoy activities for all ages!

name: Friends House
description: The Grade II listed home of Quakers in Britain, Friends House won an RIBA bronze medal in 1927. The building houses the central offices of Quakers in Britain as well as their library and archive, event spaces, a café, bookshop, worship space, courtyard, and garden. Friends House serves as a hub for an array of events, meetings, conferences, and gatherings for organisations and individuals.

name: From Forest to Morris: A walk around Walthamstow
description: A walk around historic Walthamstow showing how this unique area grew from a village into a thriving suburb, its social history and the variety of buildings that can be found where Epping Forest meets William Morris.
address: Outside Costa Coffee at Walthamstow Central Station 5 Station Approac

name: From Tiles to Tales: Feltham’s Mural and Mosaic Trail
description: A guided tour of Feltham’s mural & mosaic placemaking collection. Explore inclusive artworks celebrating Feltham’s rich heritage, creativity and community spirit. You will encounter tributes of Feltham’s former residents and student, Freddie Mercury, Sir Brian May & Sir Mo Farah. The tour concludes at the Freddie Mercury Memorial Garden & Eco Cabin, marking what would have been his 80th birthday.
address: Feltham Train Station Ticket Office (towards Waterloo), Feltham

name: Fullwell Cross Library
description: The library was built on an open site in Barkingside High Street. Circular library design copies nearby roundabout. Complex is set back from the pavement, to form a new local civic centre with a public space. Refurbished 1990 and 2011.

name: Gaunson Creative Open Studios part of Markfield Road Festival
description: Gaunson Creative Studios in South Tottenham, home to over 70 artist studios, will be opening its doors for the first time since 2019. Visitors will be able to meet and buy from over 50 artists across the weekend.
address: Gaunson Creative Studios, Gunson House, Markfield Road, N15 4QQ

name: Gideon Reeling’s The Soho Shuffle
description:
An original walking trail set to a celebratory soundtrack:
uncovering lively tales of secret doors, latest crazes and 300 years of entertaining Soho - from Georgian masquerades to the beat of the present day. 
A collaboration between the Museum of Soho and site-responsive, immersive theatre makers Gideon Reeling, blending digital tech with performance

name: Gongoozlers of Regent's Canal & Little Venice
description: Calling all canal enthusiasts - also known as 'gongoozlers' - to walk through the social and industrial history of Little Venice, Camden Lock, and St Pancras. If you enjoyed Gongoozlers of Regent's Canal & Limehouse Basin in the east (Open House 2024), you will enjoy this new west side story. Discover how a hand-dug canal shaped the lives of West Enders, Londoners, and the United Kingdom.
address: The Toll House, Delamere Terrace, W2 6ND

name: Good Shepherd Studios
description: The doors to the building will be opened to the public. Not only will visitors get the opportunity to see "behind the scenes" at Good Shepherd Studios but they will have the opportunity to join taster sessions from site regulars and find out more about what takes place onsite at Our Pastures Community Garden and Pastures Centre too.

name: Green Lodge
description: Green Lodge is a low-energy family home by Stylus Architects, carefully embedded into the landscape of Putney Heath. Much of the accommodation is concealed below ground, allowing the building to maintain a modest presence whilst bringing natural light into every room through a series of lightwells and rooflights.

name: Grove Lane
description: A substantial rear extension connecting the two existing patios was added to the existing fabric of this stunning neoclassical Grade II villas dating 1821. Large sliding doors and two glass roofs were added, a palette of polished concrete floor, oak joinery and Carrara marble define the area of work and leisure for this space.

name: Guildhall Art Gallery
description:
Open daily 10am-5pm. 
Regular free guided tours 12.15pm & 1.15pm on Tuesday-Sunday, with extra tours on the final Open House weekend.
Home of the City of London's art collection, & remains of London's Roman Amphitheatre

name: Hampstead Heath Pergola
description: 800ft long Grade II* listed pergola is designed in one of London's secret gardens at the rear of Inverforth House, Lord Leverhulme's London residence (1904-25).
address: Inverforth Close (off North End Way), NW3 7EX

name: Harringay Green Lanes eateries tour
description: This walking tour with a relaxed pace is a culturally immersive food journey through one of North London’s most vibrant and underappreciated culinary corridors. The area from Manor House to Wood Green is famous for rich Turkish, Kurdish, Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, bakery, café, and family-run eateries.
address: In front of, Wood Green Station, N22 5JU

name: Heatherwick Studio at Making House
description:
Visit Making House, the London home of Heatherwick Studio, a team of over 280 problem solvers dedicated to making the physical world around us better for everyone.

Explore our new exhibition and the exciting stories of London Olympia, Little Island in New York, the central business district in Xi’an, and Birmingham City's football stadium, among many other extraordinary design projects.

name: Herne Hill Velodrome
description:
Herne Hill Velodrome, opened in 1891, hosted track cycling events for the 1948 Olympics, is now home to a thriving grassroots cycling facility - hosting everything from Learn to Cycle to local and international racing events. 
HHV overcame the threat of closure in the early 2000s, and a new pavilion, designed by Mike Taylor of Hopkins Architects, opened in 2017.

name: Hidden Isleworth - a walking tour with varied buildings
description: Isleworth situated on the River Thames was earlier known for river based industries, but grand houses like Gumley built by James Gibbs 1721 remain mingling with an 18th century public house, 19thC homes and almshouses and a police station by Frederick Caiger
address: Isleworth Leisure Centre and Library, , Twickenham Road, TW7 7EU

name: Hillingdon Civic Centre
description: Discover the architectural and civic history of Hillingdon Civic Centre on a guided tour led by local history and architecture experts. Explore its distinctive design and incorporation of the old tow, marriage room, public artworks, stained glass,  iconic "Bones" artwork, Lady Hillingdon portrait and Jane Grey window, revealing how this landmark reflects Hillingdon's heritage, identity and growth.
address: Civic Centre, High Street, Uxbridge, UB10 1UW

name: Hinde Street Methodist Church
description: Hinde Street Methodist Church is a gorgeous, Grade II-listed Victorian church in the heart of historic Marylebone. The Church was constructed in 1887 with a grand pillared portico, spire and classical interior which remains largely unaltered. The entrance foyer was remodelled in 2014 to give the church a more open appearance, better reflecting the welcoming nature of its congregation.

name: Hop on, hop off Walking Tour Bus by Hullabaloo
description: Want to know more about the history of the City? Hop aboard our walking bus for fun facts and sensational stories as we wind through the local City.

name: Howard Hodgkin Studio
description: Sir Howard Hodgkin (1932 – 2017) was one of England’s most celebrated contemporary artists. Abstracted yet allusive, apparently spontaneous but in fact highly controlled, his paintings convey feeling through gesture and colour.  His former studio, converted from a nineteenth-century dairy, sits in the heart of Bloomsbury.
address: The Howard Hodgkin Studio, Address tbc to ticket holders, WC1 1AB

name: Hoxton Hall
description: Hoxton Hall was originally built in 1863 by James Mortimer, in the traditional music hall architecture style, with the intention to combine instruction with amusement.  It is a Grade 2 Listed Plus building and one of 5 Music Hall's left.

name: Humanise Spotters Guide: King's Cross
description:
Ever wondered just what makes a building interesting, characterful and joyful? It’s not just a vague sensation or an indescribable feeling. There are specific things you can look for.

Explore the buildings around you using the Humanise Spotter’s Guide, a mobile-friendly guide which invites you to look more closely at the buildings around us, and think about how they’re shaping how we all feel.

name: Ibraaz
description: Ibraaz is a London-based cultural institution for art,  culture and ideas from the Global Majority. Bringing together artists, thinkers, and communities through exhibitions, film, debate, publishing, and multidisciplinary programming, Ibraaz creates a brave space where culture fosters exchange, pluralism, and shared humanity.

name: Illuminated River Walk: Explore London’s Bridges After Dark
description: Join award-winning guide Katie Wignall on a riverside walk along the route of Illuminated River, the world's longest public art commission illuminating 9 bridges of the Thames. Journey from Westminster to Bankside in search of the hidden details and surprising stories along the Thames, and learn about how the bridges shaped this area through time and how they continue to influence London today.
address: South Bank Lion on the south side of Westminster Bridge

name: In Situ: Croydon Space Station
description: Be inspired by Croydon's space age buildings and aviation history - from Apollo and Lunar House, to Croydon Airport. Build your own models of familiar buildings redesigned as spacecrafts and transform the town centre into a space station.

name: Inner Space Meditation Centre, Covent Garden
description: Inner Space, London’s oasis of calm, welcomes visitors back for the Open House Festival. Join us over two weekends for free Guided Meditations, Personal Development talks and inspiring wellbeing workshops that support and nurture mindfulness, resilience and inner balance. Take a moment to pause in our Quiet Room, a space that will leave you feeling reconnected, refreshed, uplifted, and renewed.

name: Institut français du Royaume-Uni
description: 1939 ArtDeco Grade II listed building refurbished in 1950, then restructured and modernised in 2014. Did you know that the Institut was founded in 1910 by a woman, Marie d’Orliac? Or that it welcomed Charles de Gaulle and the Free French Forces during WWII? Learn all about the Institut’s fascinating history and gorgeous ArtDeco architecture including its Grade II listed reading room.

name: International Maritime Organization
description: The International Maritime Organization is a specialized agency of the UN, responsible for the safety and security of shipping and the prevention of marine pollution by ships. It is the only UN organization with headquarters in London.

name: Internet infrastructure of London walking tour
description:
"When trying to find Internet infrastructure in a city, it's helpful to start from the ground up – or, more precisely, somewhere just below the ground up..." - Ingrid Burrington, artist (2016)


This tour will walk you through the ubiquitous but often invisible infrastructure that enables connectivity in London, with a focus specifically on the City of London.

name: Irish Stories South of the River
description:
Let’s find out about the Irish who lived just south of the river Thames.
Their story and achievements, covering the last few centuries to recent times, incorporating local London history whilst strolling through beautiful historic parks and Georgian squares. Starts outside The Tankard pub, Kennington Road. SE11. Finishing at Kennington Park. SE11.
address: The Tankard pub, 111 Kennington Rd,, SE11 6SF

name: John Lobb
description: Founded in 1866, John Lobb prides itself on upholding its exacting standards and unique levels of craftsmanship in the creation of hand-made shoes and boots for men. See the shop transformed from a beautiful Grade II listed building to its modern look. Also a former residence of (Sir) Isaac Newton, 1696-1700, in which he lived for four years.

name: Kaymet Factory
description: The operational factory of Kaymet, a maker of trays and trolleys since 1947. A hidden 1950s building with a small yard, originally a printing works. It is brick built, with clear-storey glazing and tubular truss north-light main shed roof.

name: Kensal House, Past Present and Future
description: Walk through almost a century of housing at Kensal House, from its pioneering modernist design to the future of the neighbouring Kensal Gasworks Opportunity Area. Explore the Grade II* listed estate's architecture, communal spaces and social history before finishing in the Residents' Room with an exhibition examining proposals for the future of this remarkable corner of North Kensington.
address: Kensal House (pedestrian entrance), Ladbroke Grove, W10 5BQ

name: Kenwood
description: A striking Neoclassical villa in tranquil gardens on Hampstead Heath, Kenwood boasts breath-taking interiors by Robert Adam and a world-class art collection.

name: Kew House
description: A family home renown for it's quality of space and light, set around a courtyard and formed from two gabled Corten steel buildings connected by a glazed link.  The basement gallery will be showing Art Form, an exhibition on the engineering of 50 major artworks by Price & Myers.

name: King's College London, The Maughan Library
description: London's first fireproof building, built to house records of the Court of Chancery. Now renovated to house a fine university library.

name: Kingston Guildhall and History Centre
description: Built in the Georgian style, the Guildhall brought together Kingston's administrative functions. Purpose-built Magistrates Courts were included in the building, part of which are now home to Kingston History Centre.
address: High Street, Kingston upon Thames, KT1 1EU

name: Kingston Historic walk
description:
We are running our usual guided walking tours around historic Kingston this year. Come and find out interesting facts and stories about old Kingston. You will be amazed about how much you learn and enjoy.



Our guided tours are informative, interesting and fun. For more information about us visit: https://www.kingstontourguides.org.uk/
address: Market house, Kingston upon Thames, KT1 1JX

name: Kingston Library, Museum and Art Gallery
description: Adjoining Grade II listed Carnegie-funded library, museum and art gallery. Museum holdings range from ceramics to topographical drawings, including the collection left by Eadweard Muybridge, a native of Kingston and photographic pioneer.
address: Wheatfield Way, Kingston upon Thames, KT1 2PS

name: LUC 60th Anniversary - Chandos Park
description: This year marks LUC’s 60th anniversary. We are celebrating a legacy founded by two landscape architects and an ecologist, built on creativity, collaboration, and meaningful design. To mark the occasion, we are showcasing five projects highlighting the breadth and diversity of LUC’s work across disciplines and design approaches. Together, they demonstrate our thoughtful and impactful work.
address: Car Park in the site, off (166a) Camrose Ave, Edgware, HA8 6BZ

name: LUC 60th Anniversary - Halliwick Recreation Ground
description: This year marks LUC’s 60th anniversary. We are celebrating a legacy founded by two landscape architects and an ecologist, built on creativity, collaboration, and meaningful design. To mark the occasion, we are showcasing five projects highlighting the breadth and diversity of LUC’s work across disciplines and design approaches. Together, they demonstrate our thoughtful and impactful work.
address: Park pedestrian gate entrance at the west end, Albion Avenue, N10 1AG

name: LUC 60th Anniversary - Swiss Cottage Open Space
description: This year marks LUC’s 60th anniversary. We are celebrating a legacy founded by two landscape architects and an ecologist, built on creativity, collaboration, and meaningful design. To mark the occasion, we are showcasing five projects highlighting the breadth and diversity of LUC’s work across disciplines and design approaches. Together, they demonstrate our thoughtful and impactful work.
address: Main entrance to the Hampstead Theatre, Eton Avenue, NW3 3EU

name: LUC 60th Anniversary - TGA120
description: This year marks LUC’s 60th anniversary. We are celebrating a legacy founded by two landscape architects and an ecologist, built on creativity, collaboration, and meaningful design. To mark the occasion, we are showcasing five projects highlighting the breadth and diversity of LUC’s work across disciplines and design approaches. Together, they demonstrate our thoughtful and impactful work.

name: LUC 60th Anniversary - West Reservoir
description: This year marks LUC’s 60th anniversary. We are celebrating a legacy founded by two landscape architects and an ecologist, built on creativity, collaboration, and meaningful design. To mark the occasion, we are showcasing five projects highlighting the breadth and diversity of LUC’s work across disciplines and design approaches. Together, they demonstrate our thoughtful and impactful work.
address: West Reservoir Green Lanes, Woodberry Down, N4 2HA

name: La Sainte Union Catholic School
description: Founded in 1861 by a group of French nuns, La Sainte Union has a rich history. See the original Georgian site, chapel and its 144-year-old organ, plus modern stained glass windows by Patrick Pollen, LSU’s own orchard and the 60s extension.

name: Lewisham Heritage at Catford Library
description:
Lewisham Heritage is responsible for the collection, preservation and making available the history and heritage for Lewisham Council and its communities.
While Lewisham Library is being refurbished our Heritage Reading Room is located at Catford Library.

There will be a display of archive material in Meeting Room 2 and hourly tours of the Heritage Reading Room.
address: Catford Library, 23-24 Winslade Way, Catford Centre, SE6 4JU

name: Lincoln's Inn
description: Lincoln’s Inn is an Inn of Court and has been an association of barristers and judges for over 600 years. Usually closed to the public, the buildings within this tranquil 11-acre estate include Grade I and II listed gems (mediaeval, Victorian and Georgian architecture) with banqueting halls, a law library, a chapel, and a modern state-of-the-art teaching space.
address: The Honourable Society of Lincoln's Inn, WC2A 3QA

name: Lisson Grove Studios
description:
Lisson Grove Studios is a 1088m2 mixed use creative workspace hub providing permanent, affordable workspace for artists, designers, makers and small creative businesses.

The complex opened in February 2026 and includes 38 creative enterprise studios, a café, dance & rehearsal studio, 22 desk spaces, a meeting room, two phone booths and an exhibition space, arranged over 5 split level floors.
address: Arbeit Studios - Lisson Grove -, Daventry House, Lisson Grove,

name: Little Mouse Cheese Shop
description: Visit Little Mouse, an Edwardian shop in South Norwood with original wooden frontage and fascia that is now an artisan cheesemonger.

name: London Film School - Parker Street
description: Come and look behind the scenes at our London Film School studios on Parker Street. Based above the Garden Cinema, a stone's throw from Covent Garden, the building has recently been refurbished to bespoke studios, edit suites and classrooms for the world-renowned British film school.

name: London Film School - Shelton Street
description: Step behind the scenes at London Film School, one of the world’s most renowned film institutions. Just a stone’s throw from Covent Garden. Shelton Street was a banana warehouse, then 70s wasteland before it had a new era as a film school in London's creative heart. Our new venue on Parker Street has recently been converted into bespoke film studios. Come and take a tour and join the workshop!

name: London Fire Brigade Memorial Hall
description: Open Day: LFB's grade II listed Memorial Hall, part of the LFB's Art Deco Headquarters, opened in 1937. The hall is rarely seen by the public and contains stunning large memorials by Gilbert Bayes depicting episodes in the Fire Brigade's history and post-war memorials commemorating firefighters lost protecting London in the Second World War.

name: London Mithraeum Bloomberg SPACE
description: Bloomberg's European headquarters contains an art gallery with regular exhibitions, and a Roman temple dedicated to the mysterious Cult of Mithras, along a display of astounding Roman objects found by London Museum archaeologists during excavations.

name: London Open Form Pavilion of Air
description: A floating acoustic architecture, playfully reframing public space as an essential community engagement through sound & site mapping. Accessed by smartphone, headphones & echoes.xyz app, the Pavilion is located outside the Serpentine Gallery,. Drawing on Oskar & Zofia Hansen’s Open Form architectural concept it is one of 15 in a series including Venice, Berlin, Dublin, Bergen and Arctic Norway.

name: London Scottish House (London Scottish Regimental Headquarters)
description: A Grade 2 listed former Territorial Army Drill Hall  featuring restored elements of the original 1882 design. It has a triple height central hall with the restored wrought iron balconies and roofing.  Notable Neo-Georgian design brickwork. It is also unique in being the last ever military drill hall built in the UK.
address: London Scottish House, 95 Horseferry Road, Westminster, SW1P 2DX

name: London's Roman Amphitheatre
description: The capital’s only Roman Amphitheatre. Regular combined guided tours of Amphitheatre and Guildhall Art Gallery at 12.15pm & 1.15pm on Tuesday-Sunday. Additional Open House tours on 19 and 20 September, please see Guildhall Art Gallery listing.
address: London’s Roman Amphitheatre at Guildhall Art Gallery, Guildhall Yard

name: Lumley Chapel
description: Saxon and Medieval former chancel of parish church, preserved  after remainder was demolished in 1864. Part C11, with many important post-Reformation monuments, including those to the family of John, Lord Lumley of Nonsuch Palace.  An expert CCT volunteer will be on hand to guide you through the complex and turbulent history of this 1000 year old building and the people who worshipped here.
address: St Dunstan's Churchyard, Church Road, Cheam, SM3 8QH

name: MATT + FIONA: Croydon Skyline
description: As part of the weekend event Build /  Play / Shape Croydon, MATT+FIONA will lead a collaborative cardboard-build activity inspired by landmarks from Croydon's skyline. Visitors of all ages can help create a large scale installation using pre-made silhouette templates and recycled materials, contributing to "Croydon of the Future, Drawing on the Past".

name: Making Spaces for Memories in Seven Sisters Market
description:
Join us to explore the recently reopened Seven Sisters market in partnership with the Making Spaces Project and Wards Corner CBS.

Known as a hub for North London’s Latin American community, the market was reopened in June 2025 in this interactive event, we will gather together, remember the history of the market and collectively imagine its future.

name: Mansion House
description:
The official residence of the Lord Mayor of the City of London, retaining its 18C character, with superb plasterwork and wood carving.

PLEASE NOTE due to enhanced security measures ID will be required on the day for entry and security screening will be in place.

name: Markfield Beam Engine and House
description: A masterpiece of Victorian engineering, Markfield Beam Engine provided a vital public health facility from 1855-1964.
address: Markfield Park, Markfield Road, South Tottenham, N15 4RB

name: Marshall Street Leisure Centre
description: The recently restored Grade II listed Marshall Street Baths were constructed in the Roman Renaissance style and feature elaborate brick and stonework, marble-lined halls and a stunning barrel vaulted roof.  Features a restoration of the marble-lined swimming pool which is an exemplar of 1930s architecture.

name: Memorial Community Church
description: Formerly known as Memorial Baptist Church this Grade II listed building opened in 1922, it retains many original features. Open House will include access to the church, gallery and bell tower, and information on church history. 18th September at 7pm Lydia Thornley will lead a talk on the craft skills used in the building, and on the 19th 3.30-6pm there is a sketching workshop

name: Mirpur: Atlantis of Kashmir at the Market
description: Explore the vibrancy of Shepherd’s Bush Market through a new lens, exploring heritage and migration under the railway arches. Mirpur: Atlantis of Kashmir uses immersive projection and original composition to enliven the memories of communities from Mirpur, a region flooded in 1961 to create the landscape-defining Mangla Dam. Plus, contribute your own story of migration to our living archive.

name: Moravian Close
description: A former stable yard of Sir Thomas More's Chelsea estate, now an 18C Chapel, other buildings, and burial ground. Parts of the enclosing walls are Tudor in origin. Ernest and Mary Gillick enhanced the grounds in the 20C.

name: Morden Extension Centenary - Treasure Hunt
description: In 1926, the Northern line was extended from Clapham Common to Morden, adding seven stations designed by architect Charles Holden. 100 years later, these stations are considered architectural icons. On this Treasure Hunt, you'll get a chance to look for clues that help you learn about their heritage and how they are currently run.
address: Morden Underground station, London Road, Morden, SM4 5AZ

name: Mount Pleasant
description: A former Victorian workhouse that has been transformed through LB Camden's Community Investment Programme into a state of the art facility for 50 homeless people laid out around a beautiful suntrap courtyard.

name: Museum of Croydon
description:
Explore the Museum of Croydon and Croydon Archives:

- Join the Curator of the Museum of Croydon and the Borough Archivist of the Croydon Archives on an intimate guided tour of our stored, rarely seen collections.
- Explore our current exhibitions with our expert staff, including Grayson Perry's Essex House Tapestries and a brand-new exhibition on Croydon's Architecture

name: National Army Museum
description: Part of the Chelsea Heritage Quarter, the National Army Museum covers the British Army’s role from the Civil Wars to the modern day. Find inspiration in the stories of our soldiers and how their service shapes our world. Founded by Royal Charter in 1960, the Museum has been on the Chelsea site since 1970. Come and find out who we are and why we are here! Free entry to all our galleries!

name: National Theatre Studio
description:
Housed in the Old Vic Theatre’s grade II former annex (built 1958) in the Brutalist style, the Studio exists to develop new work for the National Theatre. The Studio is also home to the National Theatre Archive.  

Tours will include the rehearsal spaces, writers’ rooms and script library alongside the Archive strongroom where the National Theatre’s collections are housed.

name: National Youth Theatre
description:
Public Tours tours by Architect's DSDHA and the NYT team of the recently redeveloped RIBA-award-winning building, and a first look at materials from the National Youth Theatre archive, made public for the first time as part of their 70th anniversary celebrations. 

This project is supported by the Mayor of London and the National Lottery Heritage Fund.
address: National Youth Theatre, 443-445 Holloway Road, N7 6LW

name: Nunhead Cemetery
description: Nunhead Cemetery, a Grade II* listed Victorian burial ground, is one of London's Magnificent Seven cemeteries  and is of historic and ecological importance. Set on a hillside, its 52 acres of woodland provides a green breathing space offering peace and tranquillity.  Imposing tombs contrast with the tumbling headstones and carved angels peer through a covering of ivy. Visits to chapel and crypt.

name: Obra
description: Obra is Sordo Madaleno’s transdisciplinary laboratory, open library, and public living room, turning our London studio into a public-facing space for curiosity, testing, and dialogue. An addition to London's architectural landscape, Obra will host temporary exhibitions, events, and talks fostering exchange between the studio, the environments it works within, and the communities it engages.
address: Obra, Regent's Wharf - 10 All Saints Street, N1 9RL

name: Old Royal Naval College
description: Sir Christopher Wren's riverside masterpiece in Greenwich, built as the Royal Hospital for Seamen and begun in 1696 on the site of the Tudor Greenwich Palace. Occupied by the Royal Naval College from 1869 to 1998, it is now a premier historic, cultural and educational destination in the heart of the Maritime Greenwich UNESCO World Heritage Site.
address: Old Royal Naval College, Greenwich, SE10 9NN

name: Old Royal Naval College - King William Court
description: Wren-designed building completed under the direction of Hawksmoor and Vanbrugh, 1698-1712. Original wood panelling, refurbished by Dannatt Johnson in 2001 for University of Greenwich.
address: King William Court, 30 Park Row, SE10 9NN

name: Old Royal Naval College - Queen Anne Court
description: Wren and Hawksmoor building, completed 1749 when Thomas Ripley built the pavilions facing the river. Highlights include council boardroom, grand staircase and restored Portland stonework. Refurbished in 2000 for University of Greenwich.
address: Queen Anne Court , 30 Park Row, SE10 9NN

name: Old Royal Naval College - Queen Mary Court
description: Last major building on the site (1751). Original layout, timber panelling, barrel vaulting and Portland stone. Refurbished in 2000 by Dannatt Johnson for University of Greenwich.
address: Queen Mary Court, 30 Park Row, SE10 9NN

name: Olympic Legacy Masterplan
description: London’s 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games provided a catalyst for regeneration in the Lower Lea Valley. Guided by the Legacy Masterplan, thousands of new homes and jobs are now being created, stitching together existing communities across the former floodplain.
address: Timber Lodge, 1A Honour Lea Ave, E20 1DY

name: One Paved Court
description: One Paved Court is an artist-run space on a lane of early Georgian shops and houses.  In 2017, Allies and Morrison transformed an old carpet shop into a distinctive home for resident artists and a gallery with an innovative and varied programme of exhibitions. "New interventions are as few as possible, we were there to repair the fabric and to nudge it into its new role." Allies and Morrison

name: Ongéan
description:
Ongéan Ecosystem : 
Art Studios, Gallery, Performance Space, Edible Garden & Kitchen. All built and designed with 99% Reclaimed Materials by artist Adam Ge-Saelis.
address: Ongéan, Park Mews, Croxted Rd, SE24 9DB

name: Open House 18 Woolwich Road
description: 18 Woolwich Road is a listed building known as the "Lodge", and part of the Greenwich Royal Hospital the entrance gatehouse of the third cemetery now a public park the Pleasaunce. The building is now a house occupied by Artist Fran Cottell who has added an extraordinary history using the house for her own work. A glazed roof to the rear addition has been designed by Elden Croy Architect.

name: Open House Festival Hub @ The London Centre
description: Home of NLA, London’s built environment community, and located in the West Wing of the Guildhall complex, the Centre highlights scale architectural models of London: the New London Model and the City Model, in addition to a rotating exhibition highlighting key NLA projects. For 2026, the London Centre will be home to the Open House Festival hub, with a programme of bite-size talks and printed material from the Open City back catalogue available to take home for free.

name: Our Lady of the Assumption Church
description: Grade II* listed building designed by Edward Goldie, built in 1911 in the Gothic style with five buttressed bays. Church interior is simple consisting of large nave and high & deep chancel. Nave side walls show shallow-arched recesses into which are fitted finely carved oak confessional boxes and colourful altars and statues throughout. One of only two Assumptionist Parishes in the UK.
address: Victoria Park Square, Bethnal Green, E2 9PB

name: Our Yard at Clitterhouse Farm
description: Come and visit this grassroots community enterprise where old meets new in the form of the historic farm buildings alongside our crowdfunded cafe. Find out how some of these historic buildings have been saved and lovingly bought back into community use, and find out about our future plans.
address: Clitterhouse Playing Fields, Claremont Rd, NW2 1AP

name: Painters' Hall
description: Acquired in 1532 and rebuilt in 1670 after the Great Fire, the Hall was partially destroyed in 1941 by enemy action and rebuilt in a Neo-Georgian style in 1960. The original charter, portraiture and stained glass are of particular interest.

name: Parish Church of St Andrew, Enfield
description: Grade ll Listed church, that has been much added to over the 800 years of its existence. We have  recently refurbished the organ which has a fine circa 1750s wooden organ case.  The Church has an eight-bell peal still in weekly use– the oldest bell dates from 1680.
address: The Market Place, Church Street, Enfield, EN2 6LL

name: Parish Church of St Mary The Virgin Lewisham
description:
The church was rebuilt in late 15th century with some of that work still remaining to this day.							
During the Festival there will be opportunities to self-guide or to join a group tour which will include access to restricted areas such as the crypt and tower. These last about 30 min and will start on each hour with the last starting at 3 pm

name: Peek-a-Blue
description: A family home with a newly created living space with dramatic changes in height and subtly defined nooks and zones supporting contemporary family life. Punctured openings create new connections and viewpoints between and through the new spaces. These openings are highlighted in a bold, bright ultramarine blue that contrasts with the earthy palette of other new and redefined elements.

name: People's Museum Somers Town
description:
A great little museum set in the Grade 2 listed Ossulston Estate - a prime example of pre-war Social housing - based on Karl Marz Hof in Vienna.
Open Tuesday to Saturday 10am-5pm, plus Sunday 13th 12am-4pm.

name: Petty France and its environs
description: Petty France is a short street with a long history. This walk will time travel from the medieval origins of Petty France through its sensational history to its present distinguished profile. We shall study Charles Holden's 1927 Grade 1 listed  London Underground HQ, upstaged in 1976 by Sir Basil Spence's 1976 brutalist monument to modernism,  and where the original Queen Anne house was born.

name: Pif-Paf: Right To Play
description: Right To Play is a celebration and a call to action to fight for our Right To Play. With bamboo den and structure building, Puppetry interaction, a "Long Table Mud Kitchen" play and a Run, Jump, Swing sculpture.

name: Pimlico Library
description: The story of Pimlico Library reflects the wider history of the neighbourhood, demonstrating how community buildings can adapt and evolve while remaining at the heart of local life.  It is unusual in that it shares the Pimlico Academy Campus with Westminster's Adult Education Service.

name: Pioneering sustainable design for a changing climate
description: As we leave behind a sweltering summer and face climate change going forward, we must ask ourselves how we can live more sustainably and comfortably in the decades to come. This walking tour explores a variety of architectural design responses to this question - from net-zero homes and natural material, to cohesive and sustainable communities.
address: Lewante Sandwich & Bakery, 2 Agar Place, NW1 0RG

name: Polish Social and Cultural Association
description: Built 1972-74 in a part-brutalist style, POSK is the largest Polish Centre in Western Europe. It contains a theatre, the Polish Library, the Polish University Abroad, a Joseph Conrad collection, the Piłsudski Institute, Jazz Café with regular live concerts, art gallery, and art collection on public display.

name: Pollard Thomas Edwards - Diespeker Wharf
description: Conversion of a canalside Victorian warehouse, formerly a terrazzo factory, into spacious offices, garden and glazed extension with one of the best waterside views in London. Refurbished, 2022. This year’s event will place a strong emphasis on community-led housing and creative collaboration. PTE will celebrate ten years of New Ground Cohousing.

name: Pollocks House of Cards and Paper Gardens
description:
Build a towering house of cards inspired by architects Charles and Ray Eames 1950s classic building toy- with  cards specially produced from Pollock's  vintage Toy Theatre scenery.  

Create a 3D  paper garden to take home

Or join architect Ambrose Gillick to build  giant lightweight constructions.  Suitable for all .
address: Pollock's Toy Museum, unit 49 Whitgift Centre, CR0 1UQ

name: Postwar and post-welfare North London walking tour
description: This walking tour will draw comparisons between the progress and demise of the postwar welfare state. Focusing on housing and healthcare, the tour will present prominent examples from the era  and discuss ways these are being adapted to meet contemporary challenges, such as the housing crisis and ongoing maintenance. The ambition of the tour is to reassess the value of postwar architecture today.
address: Belsize Park Tube Station, Haverstock Hill, NW3 2AL

name: Prefab Walking Tour - Excalibur Estate
description:
Step back in time with a guided walk around the historic Excalibur Estate, the UK's largest surviving post-war prefabricated housing estate.

Discover why these remarkable homes were built in the aftermath of the Second World War, explore their innovative design and architecture, and hear the stories of the people who have made Excalibur their home over the decades.

name: Print Portal
description: An interactive print making workshop exploring the threshold between public and gallery space through exchange and collection. Using the gallery hatch, visitors are invited to transform found ephemera into printed artworks. Inspired by the exhibiting artists' practices, the workshop playfully turns the gallery into a machine for making art, reimagining the traces of everyday life in Hackney.
address: Hackney Gallery, 1 Lower Clapton Road, E9 0NS

name: Private House and Summer House
description: Architect/owner designed zinc clad modern extension to Victorian home. Cantilevered glass corners and large rooflights create a light-filled space with views to a contemporary garden. The garden connects the house to the Summer House, a contemporary black larch clad timber framed/ sustainable SIPS panels pavilion with views across the adjacent nature reserve.

name: Punchdrunk Enrichment Stores
description:
A unique immersive theatre space in Wembley.

Punchdrunk Enrichment creates immersive theatre experiences for families, schools and communities. Through our adventurous, high-quality approach to storytelling we champion the imagination.
At our creative home in Brent we run family theatre shows, community days, masterclasses and more. Come and explore!

name: Quaker Meeting House - Wandsworth
description: Grade II listed, this is the oldest Quaker meeting house in London. Built in 1778, it has original panelling & a minister's gallery. See flagstones from the earlier 1674 buildings. Also a secluded burial ground & garden. Free refreshments.

name: Queensrollahouse
description:
An evolving social sculpture housed in a 50s warehouse formerly occupied by Rolls Royce.  
Acquired in a semi-derelict state, its transformation was approached by the artist Henry Krokatsis as a large sculptural work,  built using found & redundant materials, balancing functionality and subversion. The building houses Refusés Gallery, Feral Institute, 22 artists' studios and a roof top canteen.

name: Queer Britain
description: Queer Britain Museum is the UK’s national LGBTQ+ museum.    Housed in a converted Victorian building in the heart of the regenerated King’s Cross area, the galleries feature over 200 objects from over 100 years of queer history.   At Open House 2026, Queer Britain’s volunteer guides will give talks demonstrating the museum’s mission to reclaim, preserve and inspire LGBTQ+ history.

name: Rainham Parish Church of St Helen and St Giles
description: Grade I listed Norman church with notable chancel arch with chevron and nailhead ornament, built by Richard De Lucy.

name: Rampayne Street Community Hub
description: Formerly home to the Pimlico Library, the building was transformed into a vibrant, friendly and welcoming community hub.
address: Rampayne Street Community Hub, Rampayne Street, SW1V 2PU

name: Redlees Studios
description:
Victorian era stable blocks which were converted to art studios in the late 1990s with National Lottery grant funding. 

The first artists took up leased studio spaces in 1995 and ‘Artists at Redlees’ was born.  

Facilities include work spaces, reception large open gallery, and three kiln rooms.
address: Redlees Park, Worton Road, Isleworth, TW7 6DW

name: Reform Club
description: Built as a Whig gentleman's club and inspired by Italian Renaissance palaces. Lobby leads to an enclosed colonnaded courtyard with complementary glazed roof and tessellated floor. Tunnelled staircase leads to upper floor.

name: Resilience in Highgate: multi-sensory walk
description: Highgate is frequently romanticised as a tranquil, affluent village. However, this 130-metre ridge served as a sanctuary for radicals, rebels, and pioneers who resisted the social, political, and design norms of low-lying London. This tour explores the history of Highgate’s non-conformists and community resilience. Narratives and architectural landmarks are paired with curated scents.
address: Outside Boogaloo pub, 312 Archway Rd, N6 5AT

name: Romans in London walk
description: Absorb the fascinating history of ancient Londinium, visiting sites where the Romans lived, worked, and played.

name: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew - Herbarium
description: The Herbarium, Library, Art & Archives building houses a working scientific collection located on Kew Green. We are excited to publicly showcase, through guided tours, our complex of historic and modern buildings, housing almost seven million preserved botanical collections, together with one of the largest botanical library, art, and archive collections in the world.

name: Royal College of General Practitioners
description: Grade II* listed building. Restored in 2012 to showcase magnificent Edwardian faience tile work, mosaic floor and other historic features in transformed modern surroundings that now provide the headquarters of the RCGP.

name: Royal Hospital Chelsea, Home of the Chelsea Pensioners
description: Part of the Chelsea Heritage Quarter, the Royal Hospital Chelsea has housed the Chelsea Pensioners since 1692. Join a Pensioner‑led tour of our grounds exploring its history and architecture from Wren to Soane. Enjoy free access to the Soane Stable Yard, museum and café, and visit nearby CHQ partners—the National Army Museum and Chelsea Physic Garden which are a short walk from each other.

name: Royal Hospital for Neuro-disability
description: The original Grade II listed house was a former Georgian villa. 3 extensions were added through the Victorian period reflecting the style of the era.  Subsequent additions reflect medical practices. An archivist will be giving free tours.
address: Royal Hospital for Neuro-disability, West Hill, SW15 3SW

name: Royal Trinity Hospice and grounds
description: Founded in 1891, Royal Trinity Hospice is the oldest hospice in the UK, set within a terrace of listed Georgian houses overlooking Clapham Common and surrounded by landscaped gardens. Join us for a guided tour around the hospice and grounds, including areas of interest usually not open for visitors.

name: Rufford Mews Apartment
description:
Home to RHS Chelsea Gold Medalists Mike McMahon and Jewlsy Mathews, this space showcases a decade of their handcrafted furniture and cabinetry. 
Their work, all made by their own hands, has received international acclaim featuring in BBC Gardeners' World (TV), The Modern House, The Observer, Dwell, Interior Design and IDEAT. Experience bespoke design in every meticulously crafted detail.

name: Sacred Grounds / St Anne's Church and Garden
description: Start your exploration of the Open House Soho Neighbourhood with a shot of coffee, a refreshing cold drink and a bite to eat.  Explore our timeline of Soho, and our existing display on the church's history.   Relax in our calm and welcoming gardens.

name: Sacred Heart Church
description: The Sacred Heart Roman Catholic Church is a Grade II* listed, decorated Gothic building on Edge Hill in Wimbledon, south west London. The church was completed in 1887 after being designed by renowned church architect, Frederick Arthur Walters, (1849-1931) who also designed St Joseph's, Roehampton, St John's Seminary, Wonersh, and Buckfast Abbey.

name: Sanderstead Library
description: Sanderstead Library, built in 1936 in the moderne style, was closed since late 2024. A year ago, it reopens for the first time on Open House Weekend as the future home of The Story Sanctuary - a creative health and wellbeing hub in the making. A year on, come down and see how things have developed, learn more about our plans for the building and the future of this precious community space.

name: Sands End Arts & Community Centre
description: Amongst the RIBA Stirling Prize shortlist 2022 sits Mæ Architect's Sands End Arts & Community Centre in Fulham. The centre consists of a single-storey building comprising bright, airy and flexible event spaces and a community café.

name: Scadbury Moated Manor
description: See the archaeological excavations and Tudor foundations at Scadbury Moated Manor - which still has its moat around it.
address: Scadbury Moated Manor, Perry Street, Chislehurst, BR7 6LN

name: Senate House
description: London’s tallest secular building when it opened as the HQ of the University of London and home to the Ministry of Information during WWII, this Grade II* listed landmark features Classicism and Art Deco elements.
address: University of London, Malet Street, WC1E 7HU

name: Shaftesbury Theatre
description: Built in a Renaissance style with high level Diocletian windows and a prominent grand cupola. In 2016 a new Fly Tower opened followed by remodelling of the auditorium in 2018 and the creation of a new basement space opened in 2022.

name: Sheppard Robson, 77 Parkway
description: Nestled off a busy street in Camden, the former industrial building has been home to architectural firm Sheppard Robson for over 40 years. A series of additions have allowed more amenity, social spaces, and diversity in work settings.

name: Simon's second test
description: sdfhjldsfhl

name: Simon's test
description: this is a test

name: Six Columns
description:
Six Columns was selected as the RIBA 2024 House of the Year. The house was designed by the architect owner for their family within their existing neighbourhood, a leafy street in South London. 
The house is discrete and considerate of the setting, but not meek in character or detail. From a distance it sits comfortably alongside its neighbours, as you approach and enter its character is revealed.

name: Slavery and the City
description: We will explore sites and institutions with direct links to the history of slavery and hear why the apologies were made in 2020, whilst wandering within the story packed streets and alleyways of the Square Mile.

name: Soho Square Gardens
description: The West End Open House Neighbourhood Festival kicks with a celebratory musical and dance performance in Soho Square Gardens, reflecting the festival theme of "Maybe It's Because I'm a Londoner!", celebrating the many communities that have come to live and work in the West End and and made London their home.

name: Somers Town - Photo walk
description:
A walk round Somers Town by locals founders  of a museum to preserve an area that feels at risk of extinction.

A Space for Us – People’s Museum Somers Town is a space to preserve local voice and the area; to celebrate an incredible ‘radical, reformers and uncommon people’s‘ histories, to record the change now, as well as to campaign and preserve local working class heritage.

name: South Norwood Library
description: The purpose-built library is a fine example of brutalist architecture. Built by Hugh Lea, Borough Architect for Croydon, in 1968 the main volume shows Miesian influence with an abundance of natural light, interrupted by a concrete cuboid.

name: Southbank Printmakers
description:
We are a friendly artist run gallery in Wells Street offering affordable, handmade fine art prints with a broad range of subjects created using many different printmaking techniques.
We aim to encourage people who have never encountered art before to experience printmaking through our regular workshops.

name: Southlands Arts Centre
description: Explore Southlands Arts Centre and discover the history and architecture of this Grade II listed Queen Anne-style building. Admire its distinctive red-brick façade, elegant decorative detailing and historic interiors, and learn how this former private residence has evolved into a thriving community arts centre, celebrating Hillingdon's rich architectural and cultural heritage.
address: Southlands Arts Centre, 75, The Green, West Drayton, UB7 7PW

name: Southwark Integrated Waste Management Facility
description:
Ever WONDERED what happens to your recycling?

Southwark's FREE fun-filled, family-friendly Wonder Day is back on Saturday 12 September 2026, 10am - 4pm.
 
Come along to our annual Wonder Day, to see our Integrated Waste Management Facility (IWMF) sort recycling using the latest innovations and meet some of the amazing experts that work behind the scenes.
address: 43 Devon Street, (off Old Kent Road), SE15 1AL

name: St Andrew's Church Leytonstone
description: This Victorian church designed by Blomfield will be open for a tour of its remarkable set of stained glass windows by Margaret Chilton.

name: St Andrew's Church N16
description: St Andrew's is a Grade II* listed church in the heart of Stamford Hill. With remarkable and unique wall paintings designed by Blomfield/Heaton Butler and Bayne, the murals were painted by Alexander Higerty. The building was completed in 1884, and the artwork after World War I when Higerty returned to create a war memorial for the fallen and a plaque of thanksgiving for those who returned.
address: St Andrew's Church, 106 Bethune Road, N16 5DU

name: St Anne's Church, Kew Green
description: St Anne's Church, Kew Green was consecrated in 1714. Built with the support of Queen Anne it has been a place of worship for the Royal Families over the centuries. The original 'chapel' has been extended many times and the church is now a little known gem in South West London with a fascinating past.

name: St Anne's Church, Limehouse
description: St Anne's Limehouse has been described as 'the finest parish church in England.' Designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor, it is Grade I listed and one of the Major Churches in the Church of England. It is home to a thriving Christian congregation.

name: St Augustine's Church
description: St. Augustine's, Kilburn affectionately known as 'The Cathedral of North London' was established in 1870. Fr. Kirkpatrick, the first Vicar, engaged John Loughborough Pearson as the architect with the result being what many consider one of his finest works. Externally in 1890 with the tower and spire it became the 2nd tallest building in London (now ecclesiastically 2nd to St. Paul's Cathedral).

name: St Bride's Church, Fleet Street
description: Wren designed building of 1675, interior lost in blitz of 1940, reopened 1957 with 'Wren inspired' interior
address: St Bride's Church, St Bride's Avenue, EC4Y 8AU

name: St George's Bloomsbury
description: St George's Bloomsbury is one of the twelve new churches designed and paid for under the 1711 Act of Parliament for building fifty new Churches, and the sixth and final London Church designed by Hawksmoor.

name: St George's Cathedral
description: A stunning cathedral in the heart of London. Discover the story of a forgotten masterpiece. Designed by Augustus Pugin and opened in 1848, the original cathedral was hailed as England's foremost Catholic church before an incendiary bomb devastated the building in 1941. Explore the history, architecture and legacy that shaped the Cathedral you see today—and discover its remarkable story.

name: St John the Baptist Church Erith
description: St Johns Church was built by the Normans and retains architectural features from this time and later periods. As well as original brasses and monuments, it also contains several artefacts from the excavations at nearby Lesnes Abbey. As an ancient parish church its story echos that of the local area, especially the Lords of the Manor of Erith.
address: St. Johns Church Erith, West Street, Erith., DA8 1AN

name: St John the Baptist Church, Wimbledon
description: St John's was designed by Sir TG Jackson in the Gothic Revival style. He later went on to design many buildings in Oxford (including Bridge of Sighs at Hertford College). One of the stained glass windows was created by The William Morris works at Merton. The fine Italianate floor mosaics in the chancel bear a great resemblance to the 13th Century Cosmetic Great Pavement in Westminster Abbey.

name: St John's Church, Ealing
description: We would like to welcome the local community to join with us to celebrate being 150 years old this year.  Inside you'll be able to see a timeline of the Church's history, including its role in the community, and other displays. Tours of the worship space and the crypt will be available.

name: St Margaret's Church, Lee
description:
The Church was built in 1839/41 as a white 'Hall-Church'. 
The 1870s Gothic Revivalism was overseen to a very high standard, by James Brooks and helped by 10 top craftsmen of the day. We also have a WWI Memorial by Violet Pinwill.
address: St Margarets Church, Lee Terrace, SE13 5DN

name: St Margaret's Parish  Church Barking
description: The parish church of St. Margaret of Antioch Virgin and Martyr is a Grade I listed building dating back to 1215. The church is the living continuation of Barking Abbey, sharing a joint history for centuries.
address: St Margaret's Parish Church, The Broadway, North St, Barking

name: St Mark's Church, Wimbledon
description: St Mark's Church is a striking, late '60s building of 5-sided, tent-like structure.
